To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in PAN nephrosis the glomerular barrier is defective in its exclusion of macromolecules, and the defect appears to be located primarily in the glomerulus.
the glomerular barrier function is altered by PAN administration in a complex way.

PAN-induced proteinuria is due to a diminution in the electrostatic barrier properties of the glomerulus, and that this defect is not due to an increase in glomerular capillaries permeability to macromolecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of the puromyci-induced defects in the glomerulus.
the mechanisms by which glomerular injury leads to the proteinuria of the nephrotic syndrome.
the mechanisms of proteinuria in the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in puromycin a nephrosis, the glomerular ultrafiltration coefficient is reduced, due to a diminution in the filtration surface area of the capillary wall, and that the electrostatic barrier of this wall is impaired, thereby permitting increased passage of polycations such as albumin and polyanions such a DS.

in PAN nephrosis, the glomerular barrier function is altered in such a way that the glomerular ultrafiltrate contains an increased concentration of polyanions and that the increased permeability to macromolecules is a direct result of the loss of the electrostatic repulsive barrier to polyanionic macromolecules.
in PAN nephrosis, glomerular capillaries are not enlarged, but are reduced in number, and that the increased permeability to albumin is due to a loss of the electrostatic charge barrier.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the glomerular barrier to the passage of macromolecules in PAN nephrosis appears to be intact, but is functionally compromised by a decrease in pore density, resulting in a reduced glomerular filtration surface area.

the glomerular barrier function in PAN nephrosis has been altered in a manner that allows a marked increase in the glomerulotubular passage of polyanionic macromolecules, but does not allow a comparable increase in the passage of uncharged or neutral molecules of comparable size.

PAN nephrosis is characterized by a marked reduction in glomerulus filtration surface area, and that this reduction in glomerullus filtration surface area is the major factor responsible for the reduction in GFR.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the increased filtration of albumin and other serum proteins in PAN nephrosis, and presumably in other forms of glomerular injury as well, is due to a diminution in the barrier function of the negatively charged glomerular capillaries, and is not due to increased effective pore size.
PAN nephrosis is associated with a reduction in glomerulus surface area.
the PAN model is a good model of glomerulopathy and proteinuria in human disease.
